Established in 2020, PINE & CO is a space designed to introduce various drinking cultures to consumers through cocktails, regardless of genres including culture, art, experience, and story.

Est. 2020
Scroll

Pine holds two meanings.

The Pine Tree

Pine tree is commonly found in Korea and is loved by many people because of its versatile usage. It symbolizes fidelity and will and is one of the Ten Symbols of Longevity in Asia.

The Pineapple

Pineapple also symbolizes and represents bartenders. Pineapple’s origin comes from pine of pine trees, and it symbolizes the inner sweet, genuine hospitality towards the customers, despite its rough surface.

Motivation

A retro house of Seoul

Pine&Co is a unique and nostalgic space that transports guests back to the 80s and 90s in Seoul. Established in 2020, the theme of the space is a “retro house of Seoul,” with an entrance design that reminds guests of the common alleyways they used to play in as children.

The space is divided into two distinct areas: the outside interior, which features retro arcade game machines and a very old-style gate, making guests feel as though they are facing a house from the 80s and 90s. To enter the inside, guests must press a retro-style doorbell.

The inside interior is a stark contrast to the outside, with a modern and sophisticated design. The lighting and music are changed daily depending on the mood of the day. Pine&Co serves drinks and foods based on Korean cuisine ingredients that are easily found in Korean markets. The establishment is always looking to give guests new experiences through collaborations with artists, chefs, designers, and other professionals.

The bartenders

Founders

Co-founder

Du Ui Hong (Joe)

Du Ui’s career in the bartending industry began at the young age of 23, honing his skills as a flair bartender in Korea before gaining experience in the culturally diverse neighborhood of Itaewon. In 2014, he joined Le Chamber, one of the top bars in Asia, as one of its opening members, and quickly rose to bar manager. His education in Korean traditional spirits at Suldoc greatly influences his approach, as he incorporates that expertise to magnify the true Korean-style essence in his cocktails.

  • 2017 World Class Korea Winner · Mexico City finals
  • 2019 Bols Around the World — Best Asia Pacific Bar Team
  • 2019 Angostura Cocktail Challenge Korea Winner
  • Diageo World Class Educator & Judge
Co-founder

Pat Park

At the young age of 24, Pat Park began his journey in the bartending industry, opening a gastrobar called ‘Billow’ in Changwon with his brother. Fueled by his passion for cocktail-making, he ventured to Melbourne to learn from renowned bartender Jack Sotti at Boilermaker House. Upon returning to Seoul, Pat joined Le Chamber as a senior bartender, rising to Head Bartender in 2019.

  • 2018 Patron Perfectionist Korea Winner
  • 2019 La Maison Cointreau Korea Winner
  • 2019 Bols Around the World — Asia Pacific Top Bar Team
  • 2021–present Bacardi Portfolio Brand Ambassador

Step back in time · 1980s–1990s Seoul
The Entrance

Press the bell, like coming home

Step back in time as you enter Pine&Co, where the vintage sign and entrance are reminiscent of the bustling streets of 1980s–1990s Seoul.

We embrace the traditional Korean custom of placing the name sign on the door, inviting guests to press the bell as if they were visiting a friend’s house — creating a warm and welcoming atmosphere.

Outside, a retro arcade machine glows beside a weathered old gate. Find the rough plaster wall, the wooden ‘파인앤코’ sign, and the little grid doorbell — and ring.

Find usSeolleung-ro 157-gil 33 · Seoul
Inspiration

The old gates of Seoul

The weathered gates and doorbells of Seoul’s back-alleys — the name plates, the worn brass handles, the old intercoms — are the inspiration behind Pine&Co’s entrance. We wanted you to feel, for a moment, like you were ringing the bell at a friend’s house in the Seoul of the 80s and 90s.

Retro-gate photography · The Scoop
Versatile

Which night atmosphere do you prefer?

At Pine&Co, we strive to create a dynamic atmosphere by changing the lighting and music depending on the time of day. Whether it’s a more relaxed, jazzy and chilled mood during the early hours, or a more upbeat and energetic ambiance with louder music later on, we always aim to read the atmosphere and adjust accordingly.

Korean Alphabet

Our seats spell ‘ㅍ’

Pine&Co’s bar section is laid out in the shape of the Korean letter ‘ㅍ’ (pieup) — the first letter of ‘Pine&Co’ in Korean, 파인.

The menu

Two ways to order

Pine&Co’s main theme is ‘born from wild ideas and little moments in life’. So is our menu. Read it as a game on your phone, or as one printed sheet in your hands.

The game menu

The menu is a game

We turned the menu into a game. Open it on your phone and it is more than a list to read: flip through every cocktail, spin up a quick drinking game with your table, or dive into a playful arcade built entirely from our drinks. One code at your seat, a whole night in it.

Browse the drinks

Every signature drawn by hand, one tap each. Picture the pour before you order — the living twin of our paper menu, easy to read in a dim room.

Drinking games

Lucky Tooth, Bottle of Fate, and more — quick party games for the whole table, two to eight players, to break the ice between rounds.

Cocktail Defense

Choose your bartender, Pat or Joe, then step onto the floor. A retro arcade where every drink becomes a weapon — level up and evolve Super Cocktails. Cocktails, made playful.

Open the game menu or scan the GAME MENU code at your table
The paper menu

One sheet, big on imagination

If the game feels too high-tech, we’ve got you. The paper menu is a single sheet, designed for simplicity in a dim room. It is structured in levels, so flavours and aromas grow stronger as you read down, with a small drawing beside each drink to help you picture the taste before you order.

The experiences and culinary culture from the city where we grew up serve as the inspiration for our cocktails.

Signature cocktails · ₩26,000

Twisted, through Korea

BADA
twisted Whisky Sour
Which means Ocean in Korean

We are thrilled to have recently collaborated with a talented artist to bring our commitment to sustainability to life in a unique and creative way. Our coasters are crafted from leftover mask fabric, a clever repurposing that reflects our dedication to reducing waste. As for our signature drink, we have crafted a delicious and innovative concoction using a fake mezcal, seaweed syrup, super citrus, and egg white for a unique and refreshing taste experience.

NURUK
twisted Whisky Highball
Which means grain yeast in Korean

Nuruk is a traditional ingredient in Korean cuisine, often used to make makkulli, a popular Korean rice wine. Its aroma is unique and varies with the grain, the fermentation, and the atmosphere. At Pine&Co, we use Nuruk to create a modern twist on the classic whisky highball. Our special way to drink it is to hold a bowl and savor the aroma of roasted barley while sipping — a true celebration of tradition and innovation.

In Korea, there’s a culture of sipping the broth. To finish the last drop, one lifts the bowl and empties it, signifying that the meal was truly delicious.
HINOKI
an ode to hot stone rice
Nurungji, remembered

Our Hinoki cocktail is an ode to the traditional Korean dish of hot stone rice. We aimed to capture its essence by recreating the experience of pouring water into a hot stone pot to create nurungji. To achieve this, we specially designed a box that creates steam, evoking the scent of the forest — not only adding flavor, but a memorable and evocative experience for our guests.

In Korea, rice is cooked in a hot stone pot; water poured over the remaining grains creates ‘nurungji,’ the crispy, toasted rice that sticks to the pot.
OMIJA
twisted Punch · our best-seller
The five-flavour Korean tea

In Korea, where punch culture is not prevalent, there is a beverage called ‘hwachae’ — a refreshing drink enjoyed collectively during hot summers, made by mixing Sprite with watermelon or other fruits, adorned with flower petals using Korean omija. Currently, Pine&Co’s top-selling item is the omija cocktail: homemade omija saccharum, cherry liqueur, Korean omija champagne, and a variety of berries.
